question.question: Use PBPK modeling to predict the bioequivalence of the reformulated Exampleamide 100 mg tablet (LOT-X) relative to the reference product Refamide 100 mg (LOT-R), leveraging the clinical bioequivalence study EX-01 (Exampleamide 100 mg LOT-T vs Refamide 100 mg LOT-R) and in vitro dissolution data for all three batches (LOT-R, LOT-T, LOT-X) in pH 1.2 and pH 6.8 media, to support a formulation bridging / biowaiver assessment for the reformulated product.
question.regulator: FDA / EMA (not explicitly stated in delivery; typical for PBPK-based biowaiver submissions)
question.approach: PBPK modeling with mechanistic absorption modeling (e.g., ADAM, compartmental absorption and transit model) incorporating: (1) clinical PK data from study EX-01 for model verification using LOT-T vs LOT-R; (2) in vitro dissolution profiles for LOT-R, LOT-T, and LOT-X in pH 1.2 and pH 6.8; (3) drug substance properties (solubility vs pH, permeability, pKa, MW, protein binding); (4) formulation compositions for all three products; (5) study design parameters (fasted dosing, 240 mL water, meals at 4 h and 10 h). The verified model is then used to simulate LOT-X vs LOT-R and predict BE metrics (Cmax, AUC ratios with 90% CIs).
question.context_of_use: Formulation bridging / biowaiver for a reformulated Exampleamide 100 mg immediate-release tablet (LOT-X) that differs from the clinically tested Exampleamide 100 mg (LOT-T) in excipient composition (reduced microcrystalline cellulose, increased crospovidone, added sodium lauryl sulfate). The clinical BE study EX-01 established BE of LOT-T vs reference Refamide 100 mg (LOT-R). The modelling must determine whether LOT-X can be considered bioequivalent to LOT-R without a new clinical study.

checklist.label: Composition of every product (qualitative and quantitative)
checklist.why: Needed to define drug product input for PBPK absorption model; reformulated product has changed excipients (MCC, crospovidone, added SLS) that may affect dissolution and absorption.

checklist.label: Manufacturing process and its changes for the reformulated product
checklist.why: Process changes can affect critical quality attributes (particle size, solid state, dissolution) beyond composition alone.

checklist.label: Changed excipient and its share in the reformulated product
checklist.why: SLS added at 4 mg (1.6% of tablet weight), crospovidone increased from 8 to 12 mg, MCC reduced from 120 to 110 mg; these changes drive the dissolution difference at pH 6.8.

checklist.label: Dissolution of every product and batch in every medium tested (QC and biorelevant pH 1.2, 4.5, 6.8) with apparatus, speed, volume, units
checklist.why: Primary input for absorption model; data exist for pH 1.2 (LOT-R, LOT-T) and pH 6.8 (LOT-R, LOT-T, LOT-X); need apparatus, rpm, volume, units to translate to in vivo dissolution.

checklist.label: Particle size distribution of drug substance in each product/batch
checklist.why: Affects dissolution rate and absorption; not provided in delivery.

checklist.label: Drug product specification (dissolution acceptance criteria, assay, impurities)
checklist.why: Defines the quality space for the model; not provided in delivery.

checklist.label: Drug substance properties: MW (salt and free base), pKa, logP/logD, solubility vs pH, permeability, fu, B/P ratio, metabolism (enzymes, fm), elimination, IV or absolute bioavailability
checklist.why: Core PBPK model parameters; delivery provides MW 412.5 g/mol (free base), pKa 8.9 (basic), solubility at pH 1.2/4.5/6.8, protein binding 97%; missing: logP/logD, permeability, B/P ratio, metabolism, elimination, absolute bioavailability.

checklist.label: Clinical study EX-01 design, dose, products and batches per treatment, fasting and meals, water, sampling times
checklist.why: Defines the simulation protocol for model verification; delivery provides: open two-period crossover, 100 mg oral, 240 mL water, overnight fast, meals at 4 h and 10 h, sampling times (0, 0.5, 1, 1.5, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 12, 24 h).

checklist.label: Individual plasma concentration-time data for all subjects and treatments
checklist.why: Required for model verification (visual predictive checks, goodness-of-fit); delivery provides concentrations for 8 subjects, 2 periods, treatments A (LOT-R) and B (LOT-T) with some missing/BLQ values.

checklist.label: NCA PK parameters (Cmax, Tmax, AUC0-t) per subject per treatment
checklist.why: Target metrics for model verification and BE assessment; delivery provides Cmax, Tmax, AUC0-t for all subjects.

checklist.label: Subject demographics (sex, age, weight, height, ethnicity)
checklist.why: Needed to build virtual population matching the study; delivery provides 8 subjects (6M/2F), age 26-40, weight 59.5-70 kg, all Asian origin.

checklist.label: Subject disposition (completed, excluded, reasons)
checklist.why: Subject 003 period 2 (treatment B) has all BLQ concentrations; subject 004 period 2 and 005 period 2 have missing late timepoints; synopsis notes 4 subjects withdrawn due to adverse event in period 2. Must clarify which data are usable for model verification.

checklist.label: Bioanalytical method details (LLOQ, validation, matrix)
checklist.why: LLOQ 0.5 ng/mL stated in synopsis; need full validation report for regulatory acceptance.

checklist.label: Client's BE statistical results (geometric mean ratios, 90% CIs for Cmax and AUC)
checklist.why: Benchmark for model verification; not provided in delivery (only individual PK parameters).
